doc.title: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards) Interview, 1948-06-09
doc.interviewee: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards)

title: Parade pranks, clubhouse ground purchase, and poker games
summary: A long fused block: a parade prank on Peniston Avenue, pulling a fire engine through member Ziggler's hothouse, buying the lot from Monroe Wilson for $225, a failed earlier lot, and Saturday and Sunday poker games run by Joe Schweitzer. It cannot be divided because the questions are fused into the answer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Dr. Dorman Church with rings in their nose. And when we struck Petit Avenue and Law Street, going up to Marfell's to make our formation, Brother Wilmer, my Brother Wilmer, jumped, there was a bunch of niggers, little niggers on the corner, and he jumped out and made like he got to grab one, and the nigger got to fits. And it was a time waking on to bring him to. Uh, Brother Simpson, maybe you can give us a few details on the time we paraded with a fire truck when you run into Brother Ziggler's garden with it. Yes, the year we paraded with the fire engine on our way to disappearing that evening, we visited Brother members of the club by the name of Ziggler, who lived on Petit Avenue and Law. He was a gardener, had a large hothouse, and it seemed like some of the boys that were pulling the engine, they took the two niggers out of the engine and pulled it in his yard by hand. I don't know what the idea was, or going in there, but anyway, instead of taking the road, they went through his hothouse. Brother Simpson, can you give us an idea what the ground for this club cost? At the cost of the ground, we perched it from a Negro brick mason by the name of Monroe Wilson, who lived right around the corner from the club on Bellcastle between Law and Lunciation, and gave him $225 for the ground. Add a small building in the back, two rooms and little shed to it, and we demolished that. Brother Simpson, isn't it true that we tried to get the lot up at the next corner of, uh, what's it? On Falmore's enunciation, and they had some hitch in the owner, the title? Prior to getting this piece of ground where the clubhouse is situated now, we tried to get a piece of ground up there on, uh, on, uh, enunciation in Vermont Street. But after an investigation, we found out there was some defect in the title, so we left the loan and bought this place. Uh, Brother Thurston, can you let us know some of the games that we had at the ground? Yes. I know. the dead eppy club. We used to have regular games at the club here every Saturday night and Sunday. Poker games. And the man that used to take charge of the poker games and run them for us was a member of ours by the name of Joe Schweitzer.
